text:
IncidentBot: PAGING: Serving runtime alert: multiple containers on gpu-pool-11 reporting NCCL timeouts and stalled allreduce across TP groups 2-4. Severity=sev2. @oncall please ack.
Jordan: acked. seeing spike in 5xx and queue growth on /generate. routing to on-call bridge.
Priya: joining bridge in 60s. what region?
Jordan: us-west2. affected capacity: 6 nodes, 24 gpus. Traffic shows slow tail latency ~8-12s and a bunch of windows of 503s.
Maya: quick log from one pod:```stderr
I0415 19:00:12.234567 1234 nccl_comm.cc:241] NCCL WARN Call to recv timed out (rank 1 -> 2)
E0415 19:00:12.234890 1234 nccl.cc:512] NCCL ERROR Unhandled system error: Timeout
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): cudaErrorLaunchTimeout: kernel may have been stuck
```
Jordan: thanks. looks like collective hangs and then container restarts/oom. any recent deploys?
Priya: no deploys in last 2 hours. Autoscaler didn't change pools. suspiciously many containers show OOMKilled in kube events.
Luc: pulling nvidia-smi on node gpu-11-2:```bash
$ kubectl exec -n inference pod/serv-abc -- nvidia-smi
Thu Apr 15 19:01:30 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100-80GB           Off  | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off | N/A |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  GPU   GI   CI        PID   Type   Process name                  GPU Memory |
|    0   N/A  N/A      23456      C   python                            78000MiB |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Luc: kernel memory usage high but not exceeding card memory, processes stuck in kernel launch.
Eve: infra metrics show inter-GPU packet drop spike on ib0 for that rack around 18:59 UTC. packet err/s up 3x.
InfraBot: Auto-remediation suggestion: cordon node gpu-11-2 and drain pods, route traffic to gpu-pool-12. Would you like me to run? (yes/no)
Jordan: hold on. we need graceful mitigation: don't mass drain until can checkpoint and shift TP groups.
Priya: immediate plan: 1) failover new TP leaders to healthy nodes (route policy) 2) increase NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to include ib1/eth to avoid flaky interface 3) restart the communicator process on stuck ranks 4) roll affected pods to smaller-model-variant as fallback.
Maya: quick config diff:```yaml
env:
  - name: NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME
    value: "ib1,eth0"
  - name: NCCL_ALGO 
    value: "ring" # fallback to simpler algo for stability
  - name: NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE
    value: "0"
```
Jordan: applying env patch to a single allocation group (canary) now. Priya start rolling communicator restarts on one TP group.
Priya: restarting communicator on serv-abc (rank 2). command:```bash
kubectl -n inference exec pod/serv-abc -- pkill -f nccl || true; sleep 5; kubectl delete pod/serv-abc --force --grace-period=0
```
Priya: pod came back, logs show communicator rejoined but still sporadic timeout messages, queue length dropped 40% on that shard.
Maya: can we route traffic for high-throughput customers to dedicated pool? which customers impacted?
Jordan: customer-impact: two PLG customers seeing degraded generation (long tails), one enterprise job timed out and retried. Support already alerted customer-success.
Eve: I'm seeing one customer job that had batch size 32 trigger OOMs; we should throttle batch or enforce per-request token cap temporarily.
InfraBot: routing change ready: move 30% traffic off gpu-pool-11 to gpu-pool-12 with gradual ramp. Approve? (yes/no)
Jordan: approve ramp to 30% over 5 minutes. InfraBot: starting ramp.
Priya: after env patch + communicator restart across 3 pods, NCCL timeouts reduced but not eliminated. stack traces show communicator id mismatch errors occasionally:```stderr
2026-04-15 19:07:44 [nccl] comm_init failed: NCCL_ERR_COMM = 8
2026-04-15 19:07:45 [runtime] fallback to single-node sync
```
Luc: hypothesis: packet drops + kernel timeouts cause rank to fall behind and other ranks spin waiting for barrier => allreduce stalls. we should bump NCCL_TIMEOUT to 900s for this pool as a temporary measure.
Maya: agree, makes sense to avoid immediate OOM restarts while we isolate network flakiness. Priya, can you patch that?
Priya: patched NCCL_TIMEOUT=900 for the canary pods. Observability: tail lat p99 reduced to 3.2s on canary, error rate down 60%.
Jordan: ok start rolling NCCL_TIMEOUT to rest of affected replicas in waves of 3 pods. Monitor memory growth.
Eve: also enabled pod eviction threshold to prevent auto-restart from kube OOM killer so we can more gracefully drain.
Priya: roll complete for pool 11. InfraBot: ramp complete to gpu-pool-12 at 30%. No new OOMKilled events in last 10m.
Jordan: status update for pager: mitigation in place (env + communicator restarts + traffic shift). customer impact reduced to low; enterprise job requeued and completed.
Maya: follow-ups: 1) run full NIC health check for rack, 2) add runbook step to prefer ib1 when ib0 errors detected, 3) add NCCl logging to include comm ids and group hashes for easier postmortem.
Luc: capturing logs for postmortem. saving kernel stack traces and dmesg from all affected nodes.
IncidentBot: Incident status changed to "mitigated" by Jordan. Incident duration: 12m.
Jordan: thanks everyone. Priya please own postmortem and action items. passing on-call to Priya for the next shift.
Priya: taking over oncall. I will open a postmortem ticket and link logs. :memo: :+1:
Eve: small note — recommend adding a periodic test that fires collective barrier across TP groups under simulated packet loss.
Maya: agreed, will add to reliability backlog.
Jordan: closing bridge. if anything spikes ping the incident channel and we'll reopen. :wave:
